newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on China rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on China rumors.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures rallied late to close higher on Wednesday, supported by rumors China had purchased a small amount of U.S. soybeans for prompt shipment, traders said.

Export sources could not confirm the rumor but said it was likely China bought 50,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans for April shipment. They said Brazilian prices were cheaper than U.S. values but a backlog at Brazil's key ports would make it difficult to book soybeans for prompt shipment.
New crop months gained on ideas winter snows will lead to widespread spring floods, jeopardizing spring planting.

"Leadership was in the old crop positions but new crop got support also on potential flooding in the upper Midwest," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "That did more for corn but the bean market has to stay competitive as farmers make planting plans."
Traders reported continued technical fund buying.
"The close was more of a technical move," said Joe Victor at Allendale Inc. "The trade wanted to keep the close above the trend line and they succeeded."
Soybeans ended eight to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher with May up eight at $8.39.
The March contract expired at 1201 CST with little fanfare. Traders said ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp and Term Commodities spread March/May while FIMAT Futures spread 400,000 bushels May/March.
Gains were capped in the nearby contracts by news ADM will close its Clarksville, Miss., processing plant through the end of the marketing year. Three other plants will reduce crushing rates.
The ADM plants join three Cargill Inc plants that will be temporarily shut this summer. Cash sources have said two other major processors have reduced crushing rates as well.
On the day, ADM sold two million bushels May soybeans. Refco Inc bought 1.5 million May and USDA Trading bought one million May, floor sources said.
Tenco Inc spread 1.2 million July/November and Refco Inc spread one million November/July.
In options trade, SAK Futures sold 250 May $8.25 calls at 28-1/2 to 30-1/2 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 77,615 contracts.
